Industry-demeaning the expansion leg while leaving the funding gate in raw form is economically defensible and internally consistent with the empire-building story, but the archive's earlier full-composite demeaning test already suggests this family's alpha is firm-level rather than sectoral, so the expected information gain over the existing winner is limited.

A legitimate but incremental crossing of two already-validated archive refinements, weakened by changing two things at once (industry demeaning *and* the lt→at issuance denominator), which will make attribution ambiguous if the result lands between the two parents.

The total-external-financing flow is close to the published net-external-financing anomaly and its numerator already appeared in the archive (InvestFundedByMarketNotCash), but embedding it in the cash-coverage gate is a genuinely informative equity-vs-generic-funding discriminator rather than a cosmetic tweak.

Cleanest proposal of the set: a single economically motivated change to the one element that generates the family's alpha, with everything else held identical to the leader so the outcome is attributable.

A three-year issuance average edges toward the known composite-equity-issuance construct and the "chronic vs episodic" framing is only partly delivered by a mean (which cannot distinguish one large raise from three small ones), but the horizon question is legitimate and turnover reduction plausibly helps ls_talpha.

The composition-versus-quantity question is a real and untested distinction, but the construction is economically self-conflicting because netting out debt issuance places heavy net debt issuers — themselves a documented underperforming group — in the predicted-high-return leg, so a weak or wrong-signed result would be uninformative about the market-timing hypothesis.

The stated MIN-conjunction collapses algebraically to the additive gate it claims to replace — since RANK(NEG(x)) = 1 − RANK(x), the expression equals min(A,B) − (1 − max(A,B)) = A + B − 1, a monotone transform of SUMRANK(A,B) — so this is a near-duplicate of the archive leader, not a new structural degree of freedom.

This is a three-way recombination of already-tested components (MA3 total external funding, net-of-current-debt buffer, asset-growth selector) whose pairwise swaps have each already been measured in generations 6–7, so it is a cosmetic consolidation rather than a new economic hypothesis, and the underlying construct remains asset growth × net external financing (Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan) with a liquidity gate.

A single-component swap on ChronicOutsideEquityDependence (gross cash gate → net buffer) whose direction of effect was already established by NetLiquidityBufferDilutedGrowth, and it is nearly indistinguishable from Signals 1 and 6 in the same batch, making it the definition of an incremental variant.

Replacing the three-year mean with TS_MIN converts "chronic dependence" from an average into a logical AND and is a substantively different persistence definition, though the three-year window is short and the min operator will make the channel largely a repurchase-vs-issuance indicator with attendant loss of cross-sectional resolution.

This is the only proposal with genuinely new economic content — funding raised in excess of real investment as a proxy for loss-financing rather than project-financing — and it is cleanly scaled, but the reasoning ignores that the closest archive analogue (IssuanceIntoCashNotCapex) produced a strongly opposite-signed alpha (+3.2% , t 3.16), so the expected negative sign is contested by prior evidence and should be pre-committed to with that in mind.

Averaging two highly correlated selectors (asset growth and employment growth) that have each already been tested against the identical funding gate adds no new mechanism, while the emp-driven coverage loss makes any change hard to attribute to economics rather than sample composition.

Stacking the three best-performing components selected on their own in-sample results is a kitchen-sink consolidation with no new hypothesis and a high risk of overfitting the archive; the stated "isolates the marginal value of industry demeaning" claim is also undercut by the fact that it differs from Signal 2 by exactly one operator, making the pair a within-batch redundancy.

Purging cash from the growth selector is a legitimate and previously untested identification fix (the issuance proceeds mechanically sit inside the archive's selector), and it is the only proposal here whose change is motivated by construction rather than taste — though the resulting composite still stacks three well-known anomalies (asset growth, net share issuance, cash holdings) and the supporting appeal to IssuanceIntoCashNotCapex is a loose reading of a differently-constructed signal.

Swapping the coverage denominator from total liabilities to interest-bearing debt is a cosmetic parameter change in a gate the archive has already shown to be insensitive to three numerator variants (all producing ~-0.045 alpha), and it introduces an undefined/exploding ratio for debt-free firms that will selectively drop the least-constrained population rather than rank it.

This simply bolts the TS_MIN persistence device already tested in EveryYearIssuerExpansion onto the non-cash growth selector of Proposal 1, changing two things at once in a family that already contains a multi-year expansion variant (MultiYearCapacityProgramOnOutsideMoney), so it adds no new mechanism and confounds attribution.

Replacing the issuance-quantity channel with per-share book value accretion is the one proposal that genuinely moves the funding leg away from the published net-issuance anomaly, but the archive's generation-1 slope (fmb -1.55 with the opposite expected sign) already leans against this direction, book equity per share is ill-behaved for negative-equity firms, and there is a real risk the result is just the cash gate re-expressed with an RMW-like tilt.

The debt version of exactly this conjunction (BorrowedDistributionsWhileExpanding) already failed with the wrong-signed alpha, and the equity version's high-scoring population — cash-poor, growing, dividend-paying issuers — is largely REITs and utilities, so the signal is more likely a sector-composition proxy than a measure of externally financed distributions.

A one-function wrapper is a thin "signal," but the attribution question it settles is the right one and directly addresses the standing concern that the cash/liabilities gate sorts on permanent industry type; it is worth running as a diagnostic, with the understanding that a surviving alpha is a robustness result rather than a new mechanism.
